collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HONESTY AND ACCOUNTABILITY (HON-01 to HON-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Small lies, kind fibs, things left unsaid, things forgotten, honest mistakes and the odd careless one. Consequences stay the size of the mistake. Privacy is not lying, truth doesn't automatically fix things, and nobody has to confess, apologize or forgive.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: Two children tracked mud through an elder's clean hut while chasing a frog: own up together, or take all the blame.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) ran right through the freshly swept hut of (elder), an elder, with muddy feet, chasing a frog. (elder) came home to two clear sets of small muddy footprints across the clean floor, and a frog sitting in the water jar. Now (elder) is standing outside asking who did it. (friend) has gone very quiet.

choices.label: Say It Was Both of You

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "It was us," says (subject). "Both of us. We were chasing a frog." (friend) nods very hard. (elder) looks at the footprints, then at the two of them, and hands each of them a broom. They sweep until the floor shines, and carry the frog back to the stream. At the end (elder) gives them each a piece of fruit. That's the end of it.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: "It was just me," says (subject). (elder) looks down at the two sets of footprints, which are clearly two different sizes. "Both of these?" (subject) looks at (subject.his/her) feet. "...I've got a big foot and a small foot." (friend) bursts out laughing and owns up. (elder), trying very hard not to laugh as well, hands each of them a broom.
